title: Canonical comparisons between successive smooth etale chart sources
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient setting $P$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\ge1$, of [def-pur-conventions]. Use the actual finite exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], section invariants [def-pur-section-invariant], normal cones [def-pur-normal-bundle], and the canonical diagonal chart data [def-pur-diagonal-dnc-chart-data]. This definition extends the canonical chart comparisons to successive smooth chart sources, not only to affine-space targets.

Let $g:X\to Y$ and $h:U\to Y$ be separated quasi-compact smooth morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $e:U\to X$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $eg=h$. Put $W_U=U\times_YU$, $W_X=X\times_YX$, with first projections $p_U,p_X$, diagonals $s_U,s_X$, $m=e\times e:W_U\to W_X$, and $M=W_X\times_XU$. The map $a:W_U\to M$ is the pullback lift of $(m,p_U)$; its first projection is $m$ and $mp_X=p_Ue$. It is etale, separated, quasi-compact, and takes $s_U$ to the base change of $s_X$. These geometric typing assertions, and the projection equation defining the lift, are included in this construction. For a finite-type $k$-structure $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, define $q_e:C(p_U,s_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*C(p_X,s_X)$ by inverse etale restriction along $a$ followed by inverse smooth section base change, then the canonical etale/pro-etale comparison. The restriction is the counit-normalized one of [lem-pur-section-etale-restriction-coherence], using a graph-normalized compact-support presentation [def-sp-etale-compact-support-normalization].

The map $m$ pulls the diagonal ideal into the diagonal ideal, on every affine restriction. Define the extended-Rees map by $t\mapsto t$, $f/t\mapsto e^*f/t$. Its restriction to the zero fibre, formed by the actual zero-fibre pullback universal property, is $n_e:N_{s_U/W_U}\to N_{s_X/W_X}$. The zero-fibre compatibility needed for this lift is included as a typing assertion. The map $n_e$ gives a Cartesian normal-bundle square over $e$ and preserves zero sections; its degree-one map is $[f]\mapsto[e^*f]$. Define $r_e:C(\pi_{N_U},0)\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*C(\pi_{N_X},0)$ by inverse smooth exceptional section base change for this actual normal square and the canonical site comparisons. These geometric assertions and no unspecified map are inputs to the construction.

Put $\omega_g=Rg^!A_Y$. For separated finite-type $e$ as above define $c_e$ to be precisely the standing morphism $c_{g,e,A_Y}$ of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition], not an unspecified isomorphism. Define $\rho_e$ at $\omega_g$ by the counit-normalized etale adjoint-locality identification with its comparison-unit isomorphisms. Define $\epsilon_e:\omega_{eg}\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*\omega_g$ by inverse counit-normalized etale locality, transported by the same site comparisons. Equality $eg=h$ acts only through the equality-induced dualizing isomorphism. The ordinary normalization presentations are parameters to these constructions, never an orientation choice.

For an affine scheme $V$, define a chart of dimension $d$ to be an affine scheme $X$ with an etale coordinate map $X\to\mathbf A^d_V$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Its projection is the coordinate map followed by standard projection; its local finite type and smoothness of pure dimension $d$ are the corresponding composition facts. A chart map is an etale map of its affine sources over $V$. Identity and composition are those of scheme morphisms. The standard chart has source $\mathbf A^d_V$ and identity coordinates, and every chart has its coordinate map to this standard chart. For these charts name $C_g$, $C_{N_g}$, $\alpha_g$, $q_e$, $r_e$, $\epsilon_e$ as just defined, and name $\delta_g$ as the unique normalized DNC comparison of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]. Finally $Re_!\omega_{eg}$ means the actual compact-support value, for the domain assertion in the coherence theorem. No orientation is part of any chart or chart map.

The coefficient unit and counit-preserving etale exceptional identification are exactly the constructions of [def-pur-chart-coefficient-adjoint-data]. For $X=\mathbf A^d_Y$ and $g=p$, the self-product map, intermediate pullback lift, extended-Rees map, zero-fibre normal map, ordinary source comparison, pro-etale source comparison and normal comparison are equal to the corresponding canonical affine-chart constructions of [def-pur-chart-affine-comparison-data], for every normalized presentation $N$. These seven equalities identify the specialization, rather than introducing second choices of $q_e$ or $r_e$.

proof.text: The pullback.map projection equation proves selfMap_fst. Exhibit sourceLift as the base change of e along the second projection of the intermediate pullback, using the universal property twice. Etaleness follows by base change; separatedness and quasi-compactness follow by cancellation against the intermediate projection. The two projections prove the diagonal equation.

proof.text: Functoriality of closed-immersion kernels gives the diagonal-ideal bound on every affine open. The coefficientwise deformationSpaceMap projection equation and the zero-fibre pullback equation prove normalCondition. These use the prescribed coefficient map, without choosing a comparison isomorphism.

proof.text: Reuse the proved general chartGeometry helper from ChartNormalDifferential to remove the complementary off-diagonal components, producing an etale Cartesian centre square with ambient O. For any flat Cartesian square of closed centres, construct the normal comparison by the coefficientwise t-quotient data zeroPairData of SectionReesBaseChangeEtale. On affine opens flatness identifies the extended Rees base change as a ring pushout; quotienting by t and gluing yields the Cartesian normal square. Cancel the Cartesian centre square to obtain the projections to the centres, and use pairMap_compatible to identify the zero sections. Apply this both to O in the full self-product (identity base) and to O mapping to the target self-product. The first normal comparison is an isomorphism. Check composition of Rees maps on affine opens with the intermediate affine image under the open immersion; the ring maps compose by extendedReesAlgebraMap_comp and appLE_comp_appLE. The closed zero-fibre inclusion then identifies the composite normal map with the specified normalMap. Transport the second normal square and its zero sections through the first comparison isomorphism.
